questions.question: Why compute binary cross-entropy from logits?
options: It avoids unstable probability and logarithm intermediates
It removes the need for held-out evaluation
questions.explanation: A logits-based implementation can stay finite for confident mistakes even when probabilities round to zero or one. It does not fix a poor model.
optionFeedback: Numerical stability avoids overflow and cancellation. It does not guarantee that the learned decision boundary classifies every example correctly.
A logits-based implementation can stay finite for confident mistakes even when probabilities round to zero or one. It does not fix a poor model.
A stable loss is still a training objective. You need held-out data to estimate generalization and choose model settings.
